turns.q: What is our data protection position, and what does the DPDP Act require of a data fiduciary?

The important distinction is that a contractual Data Processing Agreement (DPA) and the statutory DPDP Act are not the same thing, as a DPA is a contractual document while the DPDP Act is the statutory framework governing what such a document must contain [1]. Additionally, company policy establishes that no standalone DPA currently exists [2]. Regarding the current company position, the customer is typically the Data Fiduciary for its own hosted content, while Leapswitch/CloudPe is typically the Data Processor for that content [2]. The company position applies the Data Fiduciary/Processor framework, a 6-hour CERT-In-aligned reporting posture from detection where applicable, and retention periods including 180-day logs and 5-year customer registration [2][3]. Cross-border data transfer conditions beyond India residency for India-designated services are not currently addressed in an approved company document [4]. Regarding what the law says, every Data Fiduciary shall prominently publish on its website or app, and mention in every response to a Data Principal's communication, the business contact information of the Data Protection Officer or an authorized person [5]. Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025, the Central Government may require any Data Fiduciary to furnish information within a specified period, and may restrict disclosing this request if it affects the sovereignty, integrity, or security of the State [6]. According to the company's reading of the law, a Data Fiduciary classified as a Significant Data Fiduciary faces additional governance obligations under Section 10 of the DPDP Act 2023, and the Data Protection Board of India may impose a monetary penalty up to ₹150 crore for non-fulfilment [7]. Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025, a Significant Data Fiduciary shall undertake a Data Protection Impact Assessment and an audit once every twelve months, submit the resulting report to the Board, observe due diligence regarding technical measures, and restrict the transfer of specified personal data outside India [8]. The company's reading of the law notes that Section 10 of the DPDP Act 2023 is not yet in force and commences on 13 May 2027 [7]. What is missing from the available sources is an approved company document covering cross-border transfer conditions beyond India residency, as well as an established determination of whether Leapswitch/CloudPe is classified as a Significant Data Fiduciary [4]. turns.q: What does the Companies Act say about the powers of the Board?
turns.text:
The company position states that the Companies Act, 2013 and applicable rules and regulations made under it govern the company's current corporate matters, including board authority [1]. What the law under the Companies Act, 2013 says:
- In exercising its power or doing any act or thing, the Board shall be subject to the provisions contained in that behalf in the Companies Act, 2013, or in the memorandum or articles, or in any regulations not inconsistent therewith and duly made thereunder, including regulations made by the company in general meeting [2]. - No regulation made by the company in general meeting shall invalidate any prior act of the Board which would have been valid if that regulation had not been made [2]. - For a Producer Company, all powers specified in sub-sections (1) and (2) of section 378R shall be exercised by the Board, by means of resolution passed at its meeting on behalf of the Producer Company [3]. - A director or a group of directors, who do not constitute the Board, shall not exercise any of the powers exercisable by it [3]. - The Board of Directors of any company or any person or authority exercising the powers of the Board of Directors of a company, or of the company in general meeting, may, notwithstanding anything contained in sections 180, 181 and section 182 or any other provision of the Companies Act, 2013 or in the memorandum, articles or any other instrument relating to the company, contribute such amount as it thinks fit to the National Defence Fund or any other Fund approved by the Central Government for the purpose of national defence [4]. - Every company shall disclose in its profits and loss account the total amount or amounts contributed by it to the National Defence Fund or any other Fund approved by the Central Government during the financial year to which the amount relates [4]. - The Board of Directors of a Producer Company shall exercise specific powers on behalf of that Company only by means of resolutions passed at the annual general meeting of its Members, namely: approval of budget and adoption of annual accounts, approval of patronage bonus, issue of bonus shares, declaration of limited return and decision on the distribution of patronage, specifying conditions and limits of loans given by the Board to any director, and approval of any transaction reserved in the articles for Member approval [5].

Sources
[1] Legal Constitution L1.10 §4.1
[2] Companies Act, 2013, s. 179
[3] Companies Act, 2013, s. 378R
[4] Companies Act, 2013, s. 183
[5] Companies Act, 2013, s. 378S
